title: Automate benchmark region sweeps with reproducible manifests and stable re-run rules
creator: Jonas Weber
description:
Context
We need a reliable, repeatable way to run the benchmark matrix across regions (NA/EU/APAC where available) and models, producing a “run manifest” that can be used to reproduce any published number (and to support Legal substantiation). Today we have a mix of ad-hoc scripts + manual coordination with Fleet; variance issues are being debugged, and Marketing/PMM needs a stable cadence for report drafts.

This ticket builds/standardizes:
1) A region sweep runner that executes a model×region matrix with consistent config, warmups, and concurrency.
2) A reproducible manifest format (inputs + environment fingerprint + outputs pointers).
3) Stable rerun rules to reduce noise (auto rerun on variance threshold / flaky infra conditions) while keeping the process transparent.

Goals
- One command to run a region sweep for a defined matrix (models, regions, workloads) and produce:
  - manifest.json (schema versioned)
  - per-run raw logs pointer(s)
  - derived metric outputs (p50/p95 latency, throughput, $/1M tokens, latency/$)
- Deterministic reruns:
  - pinned runner image / dependency versions
  - capture hardware + runtime build identifiers
  - capture full benchmark config including prompt set version + workload definition
- Stability gates:
  - detect materially noisy runs and automatically rerun (within bounded budget)
  - record rerun reason(s) + keep initial attempt for auditability
- Usable by:
  - Applied ML (sweeps + spot checks)
  - Runtime/Infra partners (debugging + capacity issues)
  - PMM (traceability for published charts)

Non-goals
- Not building a long-running always-on benchmarking service.
- Not changing core metric definitions in this ticket (latency/$ normalization is tracked separately; we only wire in the computed outputs).
- Not building new product features “for optics” (we’ll only add minimal instrumentation needed to support reproducibility).

Requirements
Runner / CLI
- New CLI entrypoint: benchmark-lab sweep
- Inputs:
  - --models (comma list or file)
  - --regions (comma list or file)
  - --workload (workload preset name; defaults to “production-mix-v3” when available)
  - --prompt-set (explicit version; e.g., v3)
  - --concurrency (preset or explicit)
  - --warmup (n requests or duration)
  - --runs-per-cell (default 3)
  - --max-reruns-per-cell (default 2)
  - --rerun-policy (variance threshold preset)
  - --out (artifact dir)
  - --dry-run (prints matrix + resolves configs without running)
- Behavior:
  - Executes cells sequentially by default; optional bounded parallelism within a region (careful with cross-cell interference).
  - Writes artifacts per cell under deterministic paths (keyed by config hash).
  - Exits non-zero on any cell that fails stability gates after allowed reruns, but still writes a sweep summary.

Manifest format (schema v1)
- Single sweep-level manifest capturing:
  - sweep_id (timestamp + short hash)
  - schema_version
  - git_commit (benchmark-lab) + dirty flag
  - runner_image (tag + digest)
  - resolved inputs: models/regions/workload/prompt_set/concurrency/warmup
  - environment fingerprint:
    - instance type / GPU type (where observable)
    - runtime build/version
    - region identifier
  - per cell:
    - cell_id = hash(model, region, workload, prompt_set, config)
    - attempts[] with attempt_id, start/end time, outcome, error (if any)
    - stability_report (variance stats, rerun triggers)
    - artifact pointers (raw logs URI, metrics.json URI)
- Must be stable and backwards-compatible for the web ingestion pipeline. Any future changes require schema_version bump.

Stability / rerun rules
- Default stability gates (initial proposal; final thresholds aligned with Applied ML + Runtime):
  - p95 latency coefficient-of-variation (CoV) across attempts > 0.10 => rerun
  - error rate (5xx + timeouts) > 0.5% => rerun
  - “capacity/queueing anomaly” heuristic: p95 > 2× median of last N attempts within same region sweep => rerun (flag only if we have enough samples)
- Reruns must be recorded with explicit reason(s) and preserve earlier attempt outputs.
- After max reruns, mark cell as UNSTABLE and include in summary (do not silently drop).

Integration points
- Capacity: coordinate with Fleet reservation plan (tracked in ENG-18503). Runner should accept a “reservation label” and print the exact matrix beforehand so Fleet can reserve accordingly.
- Export: artifacts must be written in a way that ENG-18477 can reliably upload/redact and produce versioned JSON/CSV for web.
- Dockerized runner: use pinned image for deterministic reruns (work in-flight in benchmark-lab). Runner should print the image digest and refuse to run if invoked from an unpinned environment unless --allow-unpinned is set.

Implementation notes
- Config hashing:
  - Build a canonical JSON of resolved config (sorted keys) and hash it (sha256 -> short prefix) for cell_id.
  - Ensure prompt set version and model serving parameters are included.
- Artifacts layout:
  - out/sweeps/<sweep_id>/manifest.json
  - out/sweeps/<sweep_id>/cells/<cell_id>/attempt-<n>/raw.log
  - out/sweeps/<sweep_id>/cells/<cell_id>/attempt-<n>/metrics.json
  - out/sweeps/<sweep_id>/summary.json (aggregated table)
- Summary JSON should be easy to convert to CSV (flat rows) and should include: model, region, workload, prompt_set, p50, p95, tokens/sec, $/1M tokens, latency/$, attempts, stable(boolean), notes.

Acceptance criteria
- Can run a sweep across at least 3 regions × 5 models using one command.
- Produces a manifest that allows a separate engineer to rerun the same sweep and get within stability bounds.
- Auto-rerun triggers work and are visible in manifest (including reasons).
- A sweep summary is generated even if some cells fail.
- README/docs updated with:
  - how to run a sweep
  - what gets recorded
  - how to interpret “UNSTABLE”

Risks / mitigations
- Cross-run interference (queueing, kernel selection changes, neighbor traffic): mitigate with bounded parallelism + add a “cooldown” option between cells.
- Region capacity constraints: mitigate via Fleet reservations (ENG-18503) + allow excluding region(s) and resuming.
- Reproducibility drift: mitigate by requiring pinned Docker image digest and recording runtime build identifiers.

Links
- GitHub: benchmark-lab PR-4829 (Region sweep runner + manifest schema)
- GitHub: benchmark-lab PR-4855 (Stability gates / rerun-on-variance threshold)
- GitHub: benchmark-lab PR-4888 (Dockerized runner for reproducible benchmarking)
- Related: ENG-18477 (Artifact export pipeline to web)
- Related: ENG-18503 (Capacity reservations for benchmark runs)

Open questions
- Final default thresholds: do we use CoV on p95, or absolute % delta between attempts? (Jonas/Claire to confirm with Runtime.)
- Should we rerun on high p99 as well, or keep p95 as the gate to reduce sensitivity to long-tail single events?
- How to surface “environment fingerprint” in a way that’s safe for eventual publication (internal manifest will keep full details; public artifacts will be redacted downstream).

Rollout plan
- Phase 1 (internal): run sweeps for methodology validation; iterate on thresholds.
- Phase 2 (pre-launch): lock manifest schema and runner flags; require pinned image.
- Phase 3 (launch week): use the same runner to validate no material regressions and support any “fairness” questions with rerunnable manifests.
comments: 2025-05-29 (Rina Kobayashi): Started a prototype sweep CLI locally; confirming we can resolve model/region matrices from files. Biggest gap is a stable manifest schema that doesn’t require hand-editing for every run.

2025-05-31 (Vanessa Ortiz): Please make the runner print the full matrix (models×regions×workloads) before execution so we can reserve GPU pools precisely. Also need a way to tag runs with the reservation name for postmortems.

2025-06-03 (Claire Dubois): Re-run rules should be conservative and transparent. We can’t “clean” the dataset by dropping bad runs without recording why. Mark UNSTABLE if we can’t get within bounds after bounded reruns.

2025-06-06 (Noah Patel): Watch out for parallelism across cells; we saw queueing side effects change kernel selection. Prefer sequential per region, and optionally parallel across regions if reservations are isolated.

2025-06-09 (Rina Kobayashi): Opened PR-4829 with initial runner + manifest v1. Added config hashing and per-cell artifact layout. Pending feedback on what env fields to capture (GPU type, runtime build, etc.).

2025-06-12 (Sean Gallagher): Add explicit classification for failures: infra timeout vs 5xx vs client cancellation. That helps us correlate with region incidents and avoids rerunning when the failure mode is deterministic.
2025-06-15 (Rina Kobayashi): Added stability gate hooks; wired to PR-4855. Gate currently checks p95 variance and error rate; will tune thresholds with Jonas/Claire after a few sweeps.
2025-06-18 (Jonas Weber): Threshold update request: use CoV(p95) across attempts; cap reruns at 2 to avoid burning reservation time. Also require writing summary.json even when failing cells exist.

2025-06-20 (Rina Kobayashi): Landed pinned runner image integration (PR-4888). Runner now prints image digest and refuses unpinned runs unless --allow-unpinned. Updated README with ‘how to rerun’ steps.

2025-06-21 (Mateo Alvarez): Approved. This unblocks repeatable region sweeps for report drafts. Follow-up: add a ‘resume sweep’ mode keyed by manifest + skip stable cells (file a new ticket if needed).
